_doc: Shared cases for docs/pod-contract.md. client: what `box` must send. pod: what `boxd-pod` must do with a fake podman and a fake msb whose state is given (containers, sandboxes, images, vm_images, archives). podman_calls and msb_calls are regexes matched in order against the fake podman log and the fake msb log (one line per call: its arguments joined by single spaces); calls not listed may appear between them only where exact is false, and exact holds for each log whose calls key the case lists. The _absent keys list regexes no call may match. env: settings (BOXD_*) given to boxd-pod for that case only. src_files and job_files: files (name to content) made under /work/jobs/<box>/src and /work/jobs/<box> before the call (the box is boxd-2889387319). The fake podman build gives the image the id id-<cksum of the Containerfile> and prints a line on its standard output; FAKE_BUILD_EXIT in env makes it fail. archives_built: an archive of an earlier build already sits in /work/cache/images (built-boxd-2889387319.tar). archive_stamp: the modification time (epoch seconds) given to every archive in /var/lib/boxd/images. work_files: files (path under /work to content) written byte for byte before the call (a call log, a settings hook's file). files_match: a path to a regular expression that the file's whole content, without its last newline, must match. Values in env have /work rewritten to the scratch work folder. cgroup: file name to content, written into the fake build cgroup. stdout_re: a regular expression the whole standard output must match; stderr_re the same for the standard error. FAKE_NO_ACL in env: the fake getfacl lists no access rule for the build account on the device. The cases of pod report, pod calls, pod log, the call log columns and the keys that may only read (docs/designs/dashboard.md) were generated by a script so that every byte count is computed; the fake df answers --output=size,used with 1000000000 and 370000000 one-kilobyte blocks. drop_words: the words the client adds to a removal line for a `pod drop` answer (answer to words), a pure function; the pod cases of `pod drop` print the answers. A pod case with stderr does not match another line: `stderr` is the whole text. The `size from the past need` cases give no --size to a machine that has to be made, and the recorded need in the file .mem-peak of the box folder. mtimes: path under /work to epoch seconds, set as the modification time after the files are written. The cases of pod events give both snapshots of the run r1 in work_files (cache/events/<box>/<run>.start and .end) and the call log, so the differences are exact.
